course_name_original: Aplicaciones Industriales de la Tecnología Eléctrica (12736)
prerequisites: Fundamentals of electricity and electromagnetism acquired in previous courses.
Basic knowledge of electrical machines and power generation and distribution systems.
Handling of electrical units (active, reactive, and apparent power, cos φ, efficiency).
Notions of electrical safety and basic low-voltage regulations.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply current regulations (REBT and ITC-BT) in the design and verification of low-voltage electrical installations.
Size conductors and protections in connection installations, individual feeders, and interior residential installations.
Prepare load forecasts and design the complete electrical installation of a residential building.
Design isolated photovoltaic solar installations, calculating modules, batteries, regulators, and inverters.
Draft and present the technical documentation of an electrical project, working collaboratively and defending adopted technical decisions.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 1. General concepts and basic regulations
Chapter 2. Electrical equipment (switching, protection, measurement, and apparatus)
Chapter 3. Load forecasting and design of low-voltage electrical installations
Chapter 5. Calculation of cross-sections and selection of protections
teaching_methods: Group project development (Project 1: complete design of the electrical installation of a residential building; Project 2: design of a small-scale isolated photovoltaic solar installation)
assessment_rules: The final grade (N_F) is calculated as: N_F = 0.3·N_TA + 0.4·N_P1 + 0.3·N_P2, where N_TA is the average of academic assignments, N_P1 is the first partial written test, and N_P2 is the second partial written test. To pass, N_F must be ≥ 5, and both N_P1 and N_P2 (or the final exam N_EX in resit) must be ≥ 4. If these conditions are not met, the course is failed; if attending the exam, the final grade will be N_F with a maximum of 4. In the second sitting (resit), N_TA is maintained, and other grades can be recovered via a written exam (N_EX) which must be ≥ 4. The resit final grade is calculated as: N_F = 0.3·N_TA + 0.7·N_EX.
